newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan traders say Iraq bought two sugar cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Jordan traders say Iraq bought two sugar cargoes.

text.p: Iraq has bought two sugar cargoes this week of between 14,000 and 15,000 tonnes each, one Brazilian and the other European, under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, Jordanian traders said on Tuesday.

There have been no confirmed reports of any sales emerging from the December 17 tender in which European traders said Baghdad was seeking between four and six cargoes of lower quality white sugar for arrival between mid-February and early March.
London shipbrokers said on Monday that freight orders had started to emerge quoting Iraq as an optional destination for Brazilian bagged sugar cargoes.

Jordanian traders said most of the around 120 offers by international sugar houses which Iraq was evaluating were between $370 per tonne for Brazilian origin and $380 per tonne for European origin sugar.
Iraq's counter-offers of $366 per tonne to at least 10 suppliers were rejected by the suppliers as too low, Jordanian traders said.
But at least one Brazilian and one European deal appeared to have been reached, they said.
Iraq said recently it could import some 300,000 tonnes of sugar over a six-month period when it will be selling oil in exchange for food under a $2 billion deal approved by the U.N.
